Subject: Pilot billing approach for small-batch inference (context & rounding clarifications)

Hi Jamie / Kevin —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — excited about the potential for Acme to use Redwood for your on-device planning and diagnostics workloads. Before we jump into a PO, one question that regularly comes up for smaller-volume pilots is how our billing primitives interact with very bursty requests (short-requests, many small contexts) and our minimum/rounding behavior. I want to propose an explicit pilot treatment and confirm a few details so you can forecast spend.

Quick summary proposal (short):
- Pilot length: 90 days (start on sign, or earlier by mutual agreement)
- Pilot credit: $5,000 applied as an account-level credit to offset early usage during the pilot
- Billing primitives: tokens are metered per request; context length counted per incoming request body; kv/prefix caching reduces effective billed input when repeated prefixes are present
- Rounding: we round metered tokens up to an 8-token quantum for generation windows (this avoids tiny fractional billing on extremely short responses). Context buckets are not auto-broken into multiple metering units unless you explicitly send separate requests.
- Minimums: for pilots only, we can apply the credit to cover any realized minimums rather than applying per-request minimums to you directly — effectively removing the per-request minimum impact for the pilot window. After the pilot, standard minimums apply unless we negotiate otherwise.

Attached is a short MAP describing the pilot flow and a one-page billing explainer. Two asks from you: (1) confirm this approach is acceptable from forecasting standpoint; (2) can you share a small sample of your typical request shapes (avg tokens in + avg tokens out) so I can estimate burn-through?

If that sounds good I'll loop in finance/legal for a short amendment and we can sign a short pilot addendum.

Thanks —
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez

Thanks Sergio — this looks promising. A couple of clarifying questions before we sign:

1) Rounding: when you say 8-token quantum, is that per generation call? For example if our batch sends two short calls in one HTTP request, do you apply quantum per call or per HTTP request?
2) Minimums: we understand a credit will offset charges, but will our invoice show the underlying minimums and the credit as a line item, or will we just see net $0/ reduced amount? We need visibility for our procurement team.
3) Can we get a hard cap (daily or weekly) for the pilot so we aren't surprised if a faulty integration spikes traffic? Even a soft alert + auto-cap helps.

For sample shapes: most of our pilot requests are "status summarize" calls — 120 B input on average, ~350 tokens out. We also have ~5% longer diagnostic traces that are ~2k tokens in and ~800 out. We'll send a CSV.

Thanks —

Folks — forwarding Jamie's reply below. They asked for:
- confirmation on how rounding quantum applies when multiple logical calls are batched in one HTTP request
- visibility on invoices (show minimums + credit line item)
- a soft/hard cap option for the pilot

My recommended pilot terms:
- 90-day pilot, $5k account credit applied at activation
- Credit covers all billed usage; invoices will show gross usage, minimums, and then credit as a separate line so Acme's procurement can see the breakouts
- Rounding: we meter at the per-logical-generation-window level. If they send multiple logical invocations in one payload but each is a separate generation call (separate tokens/generation), we apply the 8-token quantum per logical generation event. If they intentionally bundle multiple generation steps into a single model call, that's billed as a single generation window. (Short: quantum applies per generation event, not per HTTP boundary.)
- Cap: propose a soft cap of $200/day with email alerting; hard cap can be enabled if they request it (we'll route to infra to add a service-level throttle).

Numbers based on their sample shapes (~350 out avg): my rough back-of-envelope says they'd consume ~75k tokens/week in normal pilot traffic -> ~$300/week bill rate before credit. So $5k should be sufficient cushion.

Can finance/legal sign off on the $5k credit and the invoice visibility? If legal wants different language we can frame as a pilot credit addendum rather than a permanent minimum waiver.

— Sergio

Jamie — thanks for the sample shapes and the questions. Quick answers and next steps: 

1) Rounding quantum: we apply the 8-token quantum per logical generation window. If your client sends multiple independent generation calls in a single HTTP request we will meter them independently (8-token round-up per logical call). If you intentionally pack multiple steps into a single generation operation we treat it as one window. We'll include two short examples in the addendum so procurement sees the math.
2) Invoice visibility: finance will include gross usage, any minimums (if they occurred) and a separate pilot credit line so you can reconcile easily. You'll see both the pre-credit and post-credit numbers.
3) Cap: we will enable a soft cap at $200/day with an 80% email alert. If you want a hard throttle we can enable that too but it'll require an ops ticket to toggle.

Per internal approval, Redwood will apply a $5,000 pilot credit valid for 90 days from activation. This will act as the operational substitute for per-request minimums for the pilot period (i.e., credit will absorb the impact of any minimums). We'll provide the short addendum today and can execute via DocuSign — once signed we activate and share a read-only dashboard for daily token usage and billing burn.

Next steps:
- I'll send the addendum and sample calculation (two worked examples) by EOD today.
- Please confirm whether you want hard cap enabled at activation or prefer soft cap only.

Appreciate it — looking forward to getting you onboarded.

Best,
